title: Karnataka to launch ‘Delhi Chalo’ protest if Centre fails to release drought relief: D.K. Shivakumar

ai.summary: Karnataka's Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced a 'Delhi Chalo' protest if the Centre fails to release drought relief funds before December Assembly session, citing no financial assistance received for drought relief.

facts.claim: Karnataka would organise a ‘Delhi Chalo’ protest after the Assembly session in December if the Centre failed to release drought relief funds before the session concluded
facts.quote: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday (November 28) said Karnataka would organise a ‘Delhi Chalo’ protest after the Assembly session in December if the Centre failed to release drought relief funds before the session concluded.

facts.claim: The State had not received any financial assistance from the Union government for drought relief, and that no announcement had been made on the matter
facts.quote: He said the State had not received any financial assistance from the Union government for drought relief, and that no announcement had been made on the matter.

facts.claim: Even today, the Union government has not given a single rupee, nor has it announced anything
facts.quote: ‘Even today, the Union government has not given a single rupee, nor has it announced anything,’ he said, pointing out that Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara had furnished the necessary details at a special Cabinet meeting.

facts.claim: Karnataka has already submitted a report to the Centre, drawing attention to drought-related losses estimated at around ₹62,000 crore and seeking assistance of ₹22,400 crore
facts.quote: Karnataka has already submitted a report to the Centre, drawing attention to drought-related losses estimated at around ₹62,000 crore and seeking assistance of ₹22,400 crore.

facts.claim: The State government, which earlier announced a one-time drought relief (input subsidy) of ₹2,500 each for affected farmers, has now decided to double it to ₹5,000 amid prevailing drought conditions
facts.quote: The State government, which earlier announced a one-time drought relief (input subsidy) of ₹2,500 each for affected farmers, has now decided to double it to ₹5,000 amid prevailing drought conditions.

ai.background_note: Karnataka has reported severe drought conditions with over 57 lakh hectares of crops wilting and 226 taluks declared drought-hit, prompting the state to seek ₹22,400 crore in drought relief funds from the Centre.
